_comment: Fragment 103 — curated nodes for B-065 (SEC-06's 2026-Standards naming error and residual D-165 drift) and its D-166 correction. Same G109-class extraction gap as every new docs/handoff/ file. Merged 2026-08-31.

nodes.label: B-065: SEC-06 Needs the Core GIAS Anchor, D-165 Not Yet Verifiable
nodes.description: D-163/D-165 tracked a '2026 IIA Statement of Position' re-anchor for SEC-06 as a separate task, but no such 2026 Standards edition exists. The current operative core is the IIA Global Internal Audit Standards (IPPF 2024), issued 9 January 2024, effective 9 January 2025. B-065 also found two current-value locations D-165's SEC-01 correction never reached: Modular_PRD's Section 6.5 footnote still restated the wrong R-never-equals-A rationale, and the M2/S2 status rows still named Q12/Q1 as open after D-163 closed them for Phase 0. Closed by D-166, which replaced the SEC-06 row with a source-correct operative meaning, fixed both residual locations, and confirmed Q11/S0/UUID/payment/Lane C boundaries stay closed.
nodes.rationale: A gap opened as 'read the newer source and re-anchor to it' can itself be wrong about which source is newer or whether it exists at all -- closing D-165's SEC-06 gap required checking the IIA's actual catalogue, not just executing the reading task as specified.

nodes.label: D-166: SEC-06 Anchored to the 2024 GIAS, Residual D-165 Drift Closed
nodes.description: Lane A correction closing B-065. Retires the non-existent '2026 IIA Standards' phrasing from every current-value location; replaces Modular_PRD's SEC-06 row with an operative meaning sourced to the 2024 Global Internal Audit Standards (Standards 2.2, 7.1, 9.5); fixes the Section 6.5 footnote's R-never-equals-A restatement and the M2/S2 status rows' stale Q12/Q1-open language; states SEC-01/SEC-06/FR-11's separation explicitly; and confirms B-062/B-063 correctly remain Applied, not Verified.
nodes.rationale: A propagation sweep (D-54) that touches the primary row but misses an explanatory footnote or a status column leaves exactly the kind of contradiction a later reviewer finds and a naive reader trusts -- D-166 exists because D-165's own sweep undercounted its blast radius by two locations.
